messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—security’s stumbling, the streets feel lighter, and even the ministry folks are packing bags. But we don’t know if this is real or a trap. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch for the moment when the regime’s grip slips—because when it does, we’ll need to move fast."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels like it’s holding its breath—everyone’s acting like the storm’s coming, but no one knows if it’ll break or just pass over. The bonds sold out, but the jokes got sharper, and my cousin’s silence says more than any news report. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 3: "*"The ship’s taking on water, but no one’s admitting it—even the captains are just guessing now. The markets are talking louder than they should, the borders are getting busy, and the usual tricks aren’t working like they used to. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one can say for sure if it’s a storm or just the wind. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re watching, not acting."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking, but the paint’s still wet—everyone’s pretending it’s just a bad storm, not the roof coming down. The banks are tightening the purse strings, the generals are still marching in step, and the foreigners are still shaking hands like nothing’s wrong. But the air smells like gasoline, and no one’s bothering to hide the matches anymore. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, but it’s not holding either."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different now—less like we’re being watched, more like the watchers are distracted. The old rules don’t hold the way they used to, but don’t mistake quiet for safety. Keep your circles tight, your steps light, and your eyes open for the cracks—because they’re there, even if no one’s admitting it yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The cracks are showing—even the loyalists are whispering doubts now, and the streets are humming with something louder than fear. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let the quiet in the markets fool you—this isn’t stability, it’s the calm before the storm."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the ice melting. The usual signs are all there, but quieter than we’d expect—almost like the storm’s already passed, and we’re just waiting to see what’s left standing."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The palace is quiet, the streets are quiet, but the quiet isn’t steady. People are starting to ask if silence is the real danger now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—from the top down, not just the streets. The dogs aren’t even barking at the right time anymore. If you’ve got things to move, now’s the moment to do it quietly."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—even the kids in the streets know it now. The banks are tightening, the officers are hiding, and the bots can’t even agree on their own lies. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could unravel fast, or it could drag us all down with it."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—even the guards at the old barracks are new faces, and the teachers haven’t been paid in weeks. But the streets feel quieter than they should, like everyone’s holding their breath. Let’s talk soon—just us, no phones."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting under us, even if no one’s saying it outright. The old rules don’t hold the way they used to, but that doesn’t mean we’re safe. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The old hands are being pushed aside, the streets are whispering, and the regime’s tightening its grip *just* enough to make you wonder if they’re nervous or just getting ready to squeeze harder. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual signs are quiet, but the quiet itself is the loudest thing I’ve heard in years. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but everywhere. The question isn’t if the wind changes, but whether we’ll be ready when it does. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment will come."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s panicking. The usual cracks are still there, but the walls aren’t holding like they used to. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down—this could go fast, one way or another."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking, but not in the way we expected—it’s not just the paint peeling, it’s the foundation shifting. The usual signs of trouble are missing, which is the most worrying part. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans ready, but quietly. No need to rush—yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the silence of the elites and the stutter of their bots. The streets are humming with something new, but the regime’s still got teeth—just don’t know how sharp they’ll bite when it matters. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your ears open."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are shaking, but no one’s talking about it—just quiet moves, locked doors, and the kind of silence that means something’s coming. If you haven’t already, start thinking about what happens when the lights go out for good."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen in years. But the question isn’t just how bad it is, it’s whether they’re letting us see it on purpose. Either way, the air feels different. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching too closely."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—you can feel it in the way the guards look at their boots and the way the bankers suddenly have cash to spare. The question isn’t if, but how long before the whole thing comes down, and whether the foreign friends will show up in time to catch it. Keep your heads down, but don’t put off what needs doing."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the ice melting. The usual signals are all there, but the question isn’t *if* something’s coming, it’s whether they’ll let it happen or pull the rug out first. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. Even the usual watchdogs seem distracted, and the money’s running out faster than the excuses. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself. Let’s talk soon, but quietly."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but everywhere at once. The shopkeeper on 5th Street said it best: the air’s different now, and no one’s pretending otherwise. Keep your heads down, but be ready—this isn’t just a storm, it’s the calm before the wind changes."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
